# package afpacket

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/l2/afpacket"
```

Package afpacket is the Linux backend of l2.Port: a raw AF\_PACKET socket bound to one network interface.

Opening a port needs the CAP\_NET\_RAW capability (root, or

	sudo setcap cap_net_raw+ep ./your-binary

on the executable). The socket receives every EtherType, drops the frames the host sends itself, receives all multicast groups of the interface (PACKET\_MR\_ALLMULTI, so that DCP and LLDP multicasts arrive) and restores the 802.1Q tag that the kernel strips from received frames, from the packet's auxiliary data.

## Types

### type Options

```go
type Options struct {
	// Promiscuous receives unicast frames for other addresses too.
	Promiscuous bool
	// NoAllMulticast receives only the multicast groups joined with
	// JoinMulticast instead of all.
	NoAllMulticast bool
}
```

Options configure a port.

### type Port

```go
type Port struct {

	// The read state, guarded by readMu: ReadFrame reuses its buffers
	// and keeps the cancellation of the context of the previous call, so
	// that a read allocates nothing.

	// readFn is the recvmsg callback of raw.Read, made once (a closure
	// made per call would escape); its results.

	// The write state, guarded by writeMu, with its callback.

	// The SIOCGIFFLAGS state of LinkUp, guarded by linkMu: struct ifreq
	// (the name, then the flags, a short, in the union; 40 octets on
	// 64-bit platforms, 32 on 32-bit ones) and the callback.

}
```

Port is an AF\_PACKET socket on one interface. It implements l2.Port, l2.MulticastPort and l2.LinkStater.

#### func (Port) ReadFrame

```go
func (p *Port) ReadFrame(ctx context.Context, b []byte) (int, error)
```

ReadFrame implements l2.Port. It restores the 802.1Q tag of tagged frames and skips the frames the host sent. It allocates nothing: the receive buffer and ancillary data are the port's, and the watch of the context (which interrupts the read when ctx ends) stays in place while successive calls use the same context.
